topic: Multi-armed bandit algorithms for adaptive model selection in NLP inference pipelines
final_review: The application of multi-armed bandit algorithms in adaptive model selection for NLP inference pipelines has gained significant attention in recent years (Hutter et al., 2019; François-Lavet et al., 2018). This approach enables the efficient exploration of different models and selection of the most suitable one for a given task (Ribeiro et al., 2018). The use of reinforcement learning techniques, such as those discussed in (François-Lavet et al., 2018) and (Sivamayilvelan et al., 2023), has been shown to be effective in optimizing the model selection process. Furthermore, the integration of automated machine learning (AutoML) techniques, as described in (Hutter et al., 2019) and (Baratchi et al., 2024), can facilitate the automation of the model selection process. The importance of fairness in machine learning, including NLP tasks, has been highlighted in (Caton et al., 2023). The authors emphasize the need for fairness-aware model selection, which can be achieved through the use of multi-armed bandit algorithms that take into account fairness metrics (Caton et al., 2023). Additionally, the application of data augmentation techniques, such as those discussed in (Shorten et al., 2021), can enhance the performance of NLP models. However, the selection of the most effective data augmentation technique can be challenging, and multi-armed bandit algorithms can be used to adaptively select the best technique (Pryzant et al., 2023). The use of explainability techniques, such as anchors (Ribeiro et al., 2018), can provide insights into the decision-making process of NLP models. Moreover, the application of active learning techniques, as discussed in (Cacciarelli et al., 2023), can facilitate the efficient selection of the most informative samples for model training. However, the integration of these techniques with multi-armed bandit algorithms for adaptive model selection remains an open research question (Guidotti et al., 2019). The survey of methods for explaining black box models (Guidotti et al., 2019) highlights the need for further research in this area. However, the selection of the most suitable federated learning approach can be challenging, and multi-armed bandit algorithms can be used to adaptively select the best approach (Zha et al., 2023). Furthermore, the use of data-centric artificial intelligence approaches, as described in (Zha et al., 2023), can facilitate the efficient selection of the most informative data for model training. The importance of considering the opportunities and challenges of machine learning on big data, as highlighted in (Zhou et al., 2017), must also be taken into account when developing adaptive model selection techniques for NLP inference pipelines. References: Antonopoulos, I., & Robu, V. (2020). Artificial intelligence and machine learning approaches to energy demand-side response: A systematic review. Baratchi, M., & Wang, C. (2024). Automated machine learning: past, present and future. Cacciarelli, D., & Külahçı, M. (2023). Active learning for data streams: a survey. Caton, S., & Haas, C. (2023). Fairness in Machine Learning: A Survey. François-Lavet, V., & Henderson, P. (2018). An Introduction to Deep Reinforcement Learning. Guidotti, R.
